task: RES-01 device allocations — solve-scoped device memory budget, contract-first (docs/contracts/resource-limits.md §1, §2, §3 R3, §4, §5)
question: Can a backend=gpu solve refuse device-buffer charges beyond a caller budget with an exact stop reason and a published peak, while an unset budget and every non-gpu solve stay behaviorally unchanged?

design.option: SolveOptions.device_memory_limit_bytes (unset = account but never refuse, mirroring memory_limit_bytes; 0 rejected at the boundary as invalid_options)
design.cli: --device-memory-limit-bytes N (positive integer, else exit 8) with JSON field device_memory_charged_peak_bytes
design.python: SolveOptions.device_memory_limit_bytes attribute, device_memory_limit_bytes kwarg, device_memory_charged_peak_bytes result key
design.scope: gpu::DeviceBudget installed by api::detail::run_engine on the solving thread for backend == "gpu"; thread_local current(); nesting restores the enclosing scope; the destructor publishes the admitted high-water mark on normal return and unwinding
design.choke_point: gpu::DeviceBuffer through gpu::detail::allocate_device_memory — the sole device allocator the gpu layer uses (audit: zero callers outside gpu/src/buffer.cpp and gpu/include/markov_cero/gpu/buffer.hpp); charge before the allocator, uncharge in DeviceBuffer::release, rollback if the allocator itself fails
design.accounting: live-outstanding bytes on the solving thread; refused charges never land; sticky exhaustion for the rest of the scope

mapping.budget_refusal: StopReason::device_memory_budget_exhausted (appended to the enum) -> resource_limit, failure_site device_memory_budget, suggested_recovery raise_device_memory_limit_bytes_or_reduce_the_model
mapping.hard_allocator_failure: gpu::DeviceAllocationFailure (a std::bad_alloc) -> allocation_failure with failure_site device_allocation_failure — the shared allocation reason, device-specific diagnostics (contract §4)

design.contract_change: additive: §1 device paragraph, §2 row appended, R3 extended, §4 metering-scope limitation, §5 three boundary-test rows

honest_limits: cooperative in-process refusal — not an OS or device hard ceiling; no cudaMemGetInfo consultation, so it can refuse before the device is physically full
